extraction_text: Duryodhana expresses his distrust of Vidura and argues for pursuing his own interests, advocating for building an assembly hall and gambling with the Pandavas.
Dhritarashtra expresses his dislike for conflict with stronger opponents and warns Duryodhana about the dangers of hatred and disputes.
Duryodhana persists, citing ancient gambling traditions and claiming it won't lead to destruction, urging Dhritarashtra to order the construction of an assembly hall.
Dhritarashtra reluctantly agrees to Duryodhana's plan, believing fate is unavoidable, and orders the construction of a magnificent assembly hall.
The assembly hall is quickly constructed by skilled craftsmen and reported complete to Dhritarashtra.
Dhritarashtra orders Vidura to invite Yudhishthira and his brothers to see the new hall and play dice there.
Vidura objects to the mission, warning that it will lead to family destruction and conflict among the cousins during gambling.
Dhritarashtra dismisses Vidura's concerns, citing fate and the will of the Creator, and insists Vidura bring Yudhishthira as commanded.
